questions.question: Which cloud model provides computing resources used exclusively by a single organisation?

options.why: Public cloud is shared by many customers.
Correct. Private cloud is dedicated to one organisation.
Hybrid combines models; it is not defined by single-organisation use.
SaaS is a service type, not a deployment model.

questions.explanation: A private cloud is single-tenant, used by one organisation only.

questions.question: A private cloud can be hosted in a third-party datacenter. Is this statement true?

options.why: Correct. Private cloud can be on-premises or hosted, as long as it is dedicated to one organisation.
Location does not define private cloud. Exclusive use does.

questions.explanation: Private cloud is defined by exclusive use, not by where the hardware sits.

questions.scenario: An organisation must have complete control over its hardware and security configuration, and is willing to buy and maintain the equipment.
questions.question: Which cloud model best meets this requirement?

options.why: Public cloud gives configuration-level control, not control of hardware.
Correct. Private cloud gives maximum control at the cost of owning the hardware.

questions.explanation: Complete hardware control plus willingness to maintain it is the classic private cloud use case.

questions.question: Which TWO are disadvantages of a private cloud compared with a public cloud?

options.why: Correct. You must buy the hardware.
Private cloud offers more control, not less.

options.text: Scalability limited by the hardware you own
options.why: Correct. You cannot exceed purchased capacity quickly.

options.text: Data must be shared with other tenants

questions.explanation: Private cloud trades higher cost and limited scale for control.
